small_guidance:
- Increase TILE to 8 or 16 and try BLOCK_C=64 (exact match for C=64) with num_warps=4; the current TILE=4 with num_warps=2 launches too many tiny programs for a 4×16×64×64 = 262144 output tensor.
- Add a `triton.autotune` over (TILE ∈ {4,8,16,32}, num_warps ∈ {2,4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}) keyed on (N,C,Do,Ho,Wo) so the pool/LSE kernel can pick the best config; the kernel itself is cheap so the bottleneck is launch + cudnn conv.
- Most of the 21ms is the Conv3d itself — verify channels_last_3d actually selects a fast cudnn algo (try toggling `torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=True` and benchmark=True at module import; possibly fall back to NCHW if channels_last_3d is slower for this shape on Ada).
large_guidance:
- The Conv3d (4×32×32×128×128 → 4×64×32×128×128, k=3, p=1) dominates runtime; replace it with a custom Triton implicit-GEMM conv3d kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=64-128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=32 over IC*kd*kh*kw=864, computing input offsets implicitly (no im2col materialization) and using channels-last layout so the K loop is contiguous.
- Fuse the bias add directly into the conv epilogue, then fuse the 2×2×2 maxpool + channel-LSE + ReLU into the same kernel by having each program produce a tile of pooled outputs (gather 8 conv outputs per pooled voxel from registers/shared memory if the spatial tile is sized to the pool window) — eliminates the full 4×64×32×128×128 intermediate write/read (≈64MB).
- If full fusion is too complex, at minimum write conv3d as a standalone Triton kernel and keep the existing pool-LSE-ReLU kernel; the conv alone is the >10× headroom item, and tuning the already-fast tail kernel cannot close the gap to baseline 6.7ms.
